chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Kirby disbands in Los Angeles; Hawkins helps him home
summary: Kirby's band broke up in LA, Coleman Hawkins gave him and Denzil Best money to get home, and he led a small band with Jack McVea.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Okay. Well, after Kirby, which breaks up at the end of the War... What do you do now? You start working with your own trio?

We disbanded in Los Angeles. At that time Coleman Hawkins was playing at Billy Berg's. We played at the Plantation in Los Angeles. At that time...so Billy Berg... And I came back east with...who's the drummer...? He played with Erroll, too, on the Concert by the Sea. Denzil Best. Denzil and I came east together. Coleman Hawkins just gave me some money there, man. 'You're

I could have stayed in California really, and made it. I made a lot of friends with there. Oh, I played with Jack McVea when I was there; I got to lead this band out there. I remember I played in San Diego with him at the...not the Cinderella, but one of those clubs out there.
Yeah, a small group. But I came home. One thing...
What did you mean about Hawk giving you some money?
Oh, we wanted to come back first-class, and he helped us get home. Kirby disbanded out there, and the money wasn't too cool, you know -- the money had disappeared! So he gave us (?) to get home.
